[spoiler=Earlier statement made by ATK in haste without full information: until further notice, we resume neutrality and emphasize diplomacy and the holding of a monitored referendum in Maarav]

[b]ATK[/b]

[u]Earlier Statement Made in Haste; Baladullah Calls for Peace, an End to Mizraheli Invasion of Maarav, Internationally Monitored Referendum in Maarav on Sovereignty[/u]

[i]بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم[/i]

Without really knowing the underlying motives behind the Mizraheli invasion of Maarav, and viewing it from a lens of Shamatine continentalism, we made a regrettably biased and strongly anti-Communist statement earlier. To the chagrin of those who applauded our statement, we must retract it. 

Our own country balances economic socialism with political religiously-rooted constitutional monarchism, and the pro and anti Communist factions in the HSI are often struggling for dominance over the line of national planning and policy directives. Perhaps our attempts to ride the fence, so to speak, come across to both the communist and anti-communist countries of the world as a cop out, or hiding our true intentions. 

The reality of it is that our country was traumatized by the 22 year total war between the military dictatorship and a variety of democratic, socialist, and Islamist factions from 1956-1978, during which some 3 million people were killed. Then, from around 1980 to 1998, we faced a terrorist insurgency in parts of the country, which led to another 50,000 deaths and constant bombings taking place in cities and towns including the capital city on an almost weekly basis. 

The struggle against the military dictatorship and its fascist ideology has strongly informed our politics since then, but some of the actions by revolutionary socialist groups during the civil war were also atrocious and informed our views about Communism to a certain extent. 

All that being said, we affirm our staunch opposition to the Mizraheli invasion of Maarav, and call for a negotiated settlement. However, we also strongly urge Thyven to allow a referendum in Maarav on whether the people there would prefer to remain as an autonomous region of Thyven, become an independent country, or join Mizrahel. 

In shaa Allah there can be a resolved and peaceful settlement there, with a representative government for all people rooted in religious values.

[i]Sultan Masud al-Ayyubi
Foreign Minister Abdoul Mahonomayi
Defense Minister Musa al-Yahuddiyah[/i][/spoiler]

[spoiler=An Nabai News Editorial Board statement on Qianxun involvement in Maarav]

[b]An Nabai News | Official Statment of the Editorial Board[/b]

[u]Qianxun, Get Out! Communist Meddling in Maarav Is More Evidence of Their Plot Against the Free People of the World[/u]

[i]بسم الله العزيز الحكيم[/i]

To begin, we are ashamed of the decision by ATK to change their original statement regarding what should be obviously seen as Qianxuns unwanted interference in the internal affairs of Shamatine countries. As usual, however, the overly polite and diplomatic approach in order to avoid internal conflict and to avoid potential external conflict as well at all costs is employed. 

Either way, even if the governments official line has changed, the line of this organization has not. First off, we still agree that Maarav is a part of the broader Jewish nation, represented by Mizrahel, and as such this is an issue of Thyven occupying part of the Jewish national homeland. The so called autonomy that Thyven has supposedly given Maarav is nothing more than local collaborators being given more control to make Thyven seem less obviously imperialist. We dont have any evidence that Mizrahel is a fascist state seeking control and domination over the people in Maarav. If anything, their invasion represents the liberation of the Jewish people in this part of Shamat. 

Qianxun has a pattern of being involved in meddling in the affairs of other countries around the world, most notably in Astanir. While we dont condone the previous government there, we cannot believe that this new communist government is entirely rooted in the will of the people; evidence shows it wouldnt exist without massive Qianxun support. They also have established communist parties in various countries on every continent, which they might say reflects the desires of the workers for revolution, but we say this is just a thin veneer for them to pursue their national self-interest.

Communism is banned in Baladullah for many good reasons: it is an atheist ideology invented by people who think that Paradise and a society of perfect people can be established on earth by force. The Communists establish large and powerful states claiming these will wither away, and they intensify conflict amongst classes, saying these classes will wither away. This is like taking steroids and getting deliberately in fights with people, saying that youre doing this to get weaker and make peace with people. It makes no sense.

In shaa Allah the communists will be defeated.

[i]Editorial Board of ANN
Ali Hashami, Editor in Chief
Maryam al-Marqani, CFO
Abdoullai Kanahi, Director of Publishing
Mirzai ben Hakvah, Opinions Manager
Ghassan Kharafy, COO[/i][/spoiler]

[quote=tirakan;60813603]What even is that[/quote]

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaibatsu

Zaibatsu is a term where a few large conglomerates dominate a nation's industrial and financial sectors and hold significant influence over the economy. Zaibatsu is a Japanese term and came from multiple family-owned conglomerates that controlled vast amounts of the Japanese economy from the Meiji Restoration all the way to World War 2.

In terms of UREV Zaibatsu's, it is four large companies that want to expand outside the borders of UREV because they are constantly being blocked from expanding and broken up by UREV's anti-monopoly laws. These companies will help develop other countries and even provide their own security forces to a nation, for benefits such as control over economic sectors and tax breaks. In exchange for jobs, development, business investment and economic growth you sacrifice competitiveness and economic freedom.

The knight hushed the other men into their chairs who sat only after the King did. The two younger men looked at eachother in quiet conversation to what the King said whilst the old man merely nodded.

Sir Melville spoke up, "The Prince has already agreed to the aforementioned present set terms of the treaty, he greatly believes in the factual truth of neutral harmony in both diplomacy and at the International Alliance Assembly. Sovereignty is a must that can't be easily or cheaply sold without giving up one's dignity as a nation." He intoned.

"I have not met the Prince personally but the ministry assures us that the Prince wishes for a most uneventful and peaceful reign." Ludlows said, "His subjects, and we thank him for his wishes, should get to live a life without war and strife. It's often joked Argos and Shamat are the meat in the patty of Erene, and that is something we wish to talk about against of, the idea is both ludicrous and wrong. The Prince thinks Eneas can be a jewel example alongside Lavia and Oceanice or Westmore."

"We're ready to sign when you are, your highness. We are open to photographing or filming the event for the media." The young Mister Sarsen said smiling.[/quote]
"Perfect." the King said, returning the smile. "Let me signal the guard to bring the photographer in the room." He pressed the button on the table, and the guard walked in, bowing. "Bring the royal photographer in, please." the King said to him. "Certainly sir. Is there anything else?" "Now that you mention it, there is. Bring in some tea for the Eneas Diplomatic Envoy group, if you don't mind." "Not a problem, Your Majesty, it shall be tended to right away."

Before long, the royal photographer and a royal server walked in bringing the camera on its stand and the tea. After they set everything in place, they both bowed. "For His Majesty the King and their excellencies." the server said, speaking gently, before leaving the room promptly. 

"If His Majesty and Sir Walter Sarsen could be the only ones in the first photo." the photographer said. The King motioned to his personal secretary to walk with them just out the camera's range. "Perfect. Now if the King and the diplomatic envoy could shake hands." The picture was taken, and the photographer spoke once again. "Now, if the diplomatic envoy's group could come into the picture with the King's personal secretary. Oh, and if the King's personal secretary could go to the left of the King and the diplomatic envoy to the right. Alright, now if the Secretary of the Minister of Foreign Affairs could go the left of the Diplomatic Envoy and the Representative of the Prince's Personal Staff go to the right of the King's personal secretary. Splendid." With that, the second picture was taken.

The King moved to the table and sat down, signing the document confirming Eneas' accession to the Non-Aligned Bloc. He then handed the pen to his personal secretary, who signed the document as a witness. His personal secretary then handed the pen to Sir Walter Sarsen.
